label: original-phase step right after a "p p" bigram (t>=3)
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, at t=3..8 (peak t=4), on the step right after a p was input: 98% of activation mass has prev_tok=p. Never fires in the delimiter or copy phases, or at t<3. Magnitude grows with how many p tokens came just before: the strongest activations follow "p p" (prev2_tok=p, 66% of mass), and sequences starting with u (often u ... p p) are enriched. A single p with no earlier p gives only weak activations (bottom quartile). The token at the current step barely matters. Precision is low: prev_tok=p at t>=3 alone covers 96% of activations but only 2% of those steps fire. Even the "p p" bigram fires only about 37% of the time, and false positives look much like the hits, so some unidentified context also gates the feature. Broader alternative: prev_tok=p & n_seen(p)>=2 (dev F1 0.25, mass recall 0.86).

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: prev_tok=p (+7.00), prev2_tok=p (+4.13), orig0=u (+3.77), prev3_tok=p (+2.79), orig2=a (+2.68), prev_tok=g (+1.80). Lower it: orig_idx=-1 (-6.09), prev3_tok=- (-4.18), orig1=z (-2.12), orig1=s (-1.89).
